content.text:
Only three endpoints require `ManageUsers`. All three are in the `/users` group:

- `POST /users` (add a user), at `src/UM.Api/UMEndpoints.cs:51`
- `PUT /users/{id}` (update a user), at `src/UM.Api/UMEndpoints.cs:58`
- `DELETE /users/{id}` (remove a user), at `src/UM.Api/UMEndpoints.cs:65`

`GET /users` and `GET /users/{id}` only require an authenticated user, because they call `.RequireRight("")`.

**Where it's enforced:**
- Each endpoint calls `.RequireRight("ManageUsers")`. The extension method is in `src/UM.Api/Framework/Security.cs:26`. It calls `RequireAuthorization("right:ManageUsers")`.
- `RightPolicyProvider` in the same file builds the `right:X` policy on demand. It accepts an authenticated user who holds that right, or the `*` right, which grants every right.
- The name `"ManageUsers"` is also defined as the constant `UMRights.ManageUsers` in `src/UM.Application/UMRights.cs:7`. The endpoints use the string literal instead of the constant.
- The right is seeded in `src/UM.Infrastructure/UMDbContext.cs:16`.

I only searched for `ManageUsers` and `RequireRight`, so I haven't checked whether the service layer also checks the right.
